The couple built the H3 brand together over more than a decade, and the affair allegations have dominated discussion in the creator community online in recent days. Hila's statement puts the personal fallout at the centre of a story that had previously circulated largely as rumour and commentary. Neither a detailed timeline nor a response from Ethan was included in the initial reporting, and the episode is the latest in a run of creator-economy scandals playing out in public. The H3 Podcast remains one of the most-watched commentary shows on YouTube, and the fallout is likely to shape its coverage for weeks.

articles.title: Watch Anderson .Paak and Cordae perform 'Airbender' and 'I'm On' on 'Fallon'
articles.description: Anderson .Paak and Cordae performed 'Airbender' and 'I'm On' on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Rolling Stone reports. The joint performance pairs two of hip-hop's most charismatic live performers on late-night television.
articles.body: Anderson .Paak and Cordae performed 'Airbender' and 'I'm On' on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Rolling Stone reports. The joint late-night appearance pairs two of hip-hop's most charismatic live performers: .Paak, the drummer-singer whose high-energy shows have made him a festival favourite, and Cordae, the Grammy-nominated rapper whose thoughtful lyricism has earned him a loyal following. The two songs showcase the chemistry between them, with .Paak's musicianship and Cordae's wordplay trading off across the set. Late-night performances remain one of the main shop windows for new music, and a Fallon slot is still a significant booking for artists looking to reach beyond their core audience. The performance comes as both artists continue to tour and release new material, and it is the kind of collaboration that plays well in the clip economy — short, sharp and shareable.

articles.title: Don Toliver announces sixth album 'Nitrous' with a slick trailer
articles.description: Don Toliver has announced his sixth album, 'Nitrous,' with a slick trailer, Rolling Stone reports. The Houston rapper continues one of the most consistent release runs in modern hip-hop, and the announcement comes as his collaborations with Drake climb the Billboard charts.
articles.body: Don Toliver has announced his sixth album, 'Nitrous,' with a slick trailer, Rolling Stone reports. The Houston rapper, a mainstay of Travis Scott's Cactus Jack roster, continues one of the most consistent release runs in modern hip-hop, with a new album now arriving at a steady clip. The trailer gives the first taste of the record's sound and visual world, though no release date or tracklist has been disclosed in the initial announcement. Toliver's profile has been rising on the charts as well: his collaborations with Drake, including 'Solar Eclipse' and 'Cold Shoulder,' are on the Billboard Hot 100 this week, and he is featured on Future's new entry 'Ya Hit.' 'Nitrous' will be his next full statement after a run of albums that have made him one of the most reliable hitmakers in rap, and the trailer suggests a bigger, more cinematic presentation than his recent work.

articles.title: Miranda Lambert and Ella Langley give the live debut of 'Snakeskin Boots' at the 2026 CMAs
articles.description: Miranda Lambert and Ella Langley gave the live debut of 'Snakeskin Boots' at the 2026 CMA Awards, Rolling Stone reports. The performance paired the country veteran with the night's biggest winner, a day after Langley's 'Dandelion' took Album of the Year and her single set a Hot 100 record.
articles.body: Miranda Lambert and Ella Langley gave the live debut of 'Snakeskin Boots' at the 2026 CMA Awards, Rolling Stone reports. The performance paired Lambert, one of country music's most decorated artists, with Langley, the night's biggest winner, whose album 'Dandelion' took Album of the Year and whose single 'Choosin' Texas' set the all-time Hot 100 record with 28 weeks at No. 1. The duet was one of the standout moments of a ceremony that also featured Taylor Swift honouring Brooks & Dunn, a ferocious tribute to the duo from Halestorm, Brothers Osborne and Hardy, and Stephen Wilson Jr. performing with Chris Stapleton. Langley's CMA night capped a year in which she went from rising star to the dominant force in country music, and sharing the stage with Lambert — a mentor figure for a generation of women in the genre — was a passing-of-the-torch moment. 'Snakeskin Boots' is the latest collaboration between the two, and its live debut is likely to become a staple of both artists' sets.

articles.title: Bruce Dickinson already has a new solo album and tour dates lined up for Iron Maiden's break
articles.description: Bruce Dickinson already has a new solo album and tour dates lined up for Iron Maiden's break, Rolling Stone reports. The frontman is wasting no time between the metal giants' touring cycles, with a solo run that will keep him on the road while the band rests.
articles.body: Bruce Dickinson already has a new solo album and tour dates lined up for Iron Maiden's break, Rolling Stone reports. The Iron Maiden frontman, one of metal's most enduring voices, is wasting no time between the band's touring cycles, with a solo record and live dates planned for the downtime. Dickinson's solo career has run in parallel with Iron Maiden for decades, giving him an outlet for material that sits outside the band's sound, and his solo shows have a loyal following of their own. The announcement comes as Iron Maiden pause after another long run of touring, and it shows the 68-year-old singer has no intention of slowing down. Details of the album's title and the tour routing are expected in the coming weeks, but the message is clear: the break is a change of vehicle, not a rest.

articles.title: Bruce Springsteen's historic 1988 East Berlin concert chronicled in a new documentary
articles.description: Bruce Springsteen's historic 1988 concert in East Berlin is being chronicled in a new documentary, Rolling Stone reports. The show, played before hundreds of thousands of people behind the Iron Curtain, is remembered as a moment when rock music helped crack the Berlin Wall.
articles.body: Bruce Springsteen's historic 1988 concert in East Berlin is being chronicled in a new documentary, Rolling Stone reports. The show, played on July 19, 1988 before an estimated 300,000 people in East Berlin — with many more listening from beyond the barriers — is remembered as one of the most politically charged concerts ever staged, a moment when rock music helped crack the Berlin Wall. Springsteen told the crowd in German that he was there to play rock 'n' roll for East Berliners 'in the hope that one day all the barriers will be torn down,' a line that has become part of the legend of the Wall's fall sixteen months later. The documentary revisits the concert and its context, drawing on archive footage and interviews with people who were there. It lands as Springsteen's legacy is being reassessed in a run of films and books, and as the 1988 show's reputation has only grown with time. For fans, it is a chance to see one of the great rock moments of the Cold War in full.

articles.title: Paul McCartney, Chrissie Hynde and Peter Hook lead a Ukraine benefit concert
articles.description: Paul McCartney, Chrissie Hynde and Peter Hook are leading a Ukraine benefit concert, Rolling Stone reports. The show brings together some of British rock's biggest names in support of Ukraine, nearly five years into the full-scale war.
articles.body: Paul McCartney, Chrissie Hynde and Peter Hook are leading a Ukraine benefit concert, Rolling Stone reports. The show brings together some of British rock's biggest names — McCartney, the former Beatle; Hynde, frontwoman of the Pretenders; and Hook, the former Joy Division and New Order bassist — in support of Ukraine, nearly five years into Russia's full-scale invasion. Benefit concerts for Ukraine have been a feature of the war since 2022, but a bill headed by McCartney is a significant statement, and it comes at a moment when the diplomacy around the war is at its most intense, with the Shenzhen summit producing a declaration that did not mention Ukraine at all. The concert is a reminder that cultural support for Ukraine remains strong even as the political debate over aid and guarantees grinds on. Details of the date, venue and ticketing are expected to follow, and the lineup is likely to grow as other artists sign on.

articles.title: Michael Jackson's lawyer sued by siblings who accuse him of silencing abuse claims
articles.description: Michael Jackson's lawyer is being sued by siblings who accuse him of silencing abuse claims, Rolling Stone reports. The lawsuit adds a new legal front to the long-running disputes over Jackson's legacy and the allegations against him.
articles.body: Michael Jackson's lawyer is being sued by siblings who accuse him of silencing abuse claims, Rolling Stone reports. The lawsuit adds a new legal front to the long-running disputes over Michael Jackson's legacy and the sexual abuse allegations against him, which have been litigated in various forms for decades. The siblings allege the lawyer used his position to suppress claims, though the details of the complaint and the specific relief sought have not been fully disclosed in the initial reporting. The case lands in a year when Jackson's estate and legacy have been back in the headlines, from the long-delayed biopic to the continued commercial success of his catalogue — 'Thriller' recently hit a 40-year high on the Billboard 200. The lawsuit is at an early stage, and the lawyer has not yet responded publicly in the reporting. It is the latest reminder that the legal battles around Jackson, who died in 2009, show no sign of ending.

articles.title: Evanescence finally scores its first No. 1 on a Billboard chart with 'Who Will You Follow'
articles.description: Evanescence has reached No. 1 on Billboard's Hot Hard Rock Songs chart for the first time, as new single 'Who Will You Follow' debuts in first place. It is the band's seventh career placement on the chart and fifth top 10, and the single leads an upcoming album, 'Sanctuary,' expected in mid-June.
articles.body: Evanescence has finally reached No. 1 on a Billboard chart, as new single 'Who Will You Follow' debuts at No. 1 on the Hot Hard Rock Songs chart. It is the band's first No. 1 on the ranking, its seventh career placement and its fifth top 10, a milestone for a group that has been a rock mainstay for more than two decades without topping one of Billboard's genre tallies. The single dropped a little more than a week ago and is the first big single from the band's upcoming album 'Sanctuary,' expected in mid-June, following their 2025 return with the song 'Afterlife.' The chart frame is a crowded one for hard rock: soloist Bilmuri fills nine spaces on the Hot Hard Rock Songs tally this week with multiple tunes from his new album 'Kind of Hard Launch.' Evanescence's breakthrough comes as rock acts continue to find new life on Billboard's genre charts, and the band's return to the top of a Billboard ranking is a notable late-career first.

articles.title: beabadoobee announces surprise new album 'Bananas 4 Cats' — her second LP in under a year
articles.description: beabadoobee has announced a surprise new album, 'Bananas 4 Cats,' due February 19, with lead single 'No Punctuation' out now. It arrives less than six months after 'Pylon,' which made a top-10 debut on the Billboard 200 and earned her a second consecutive UK No. 1 album.
articles.body: beabadoobee has announced a surprise new album, 'Bananas 4 Cats,' due February 19 via Dirty Hit/Interscope, with lead single 'No Punctuation' out now. The album arrives less than six months after 'Pylon,' released in September, which made a top-10 debut on the Billboard 200 and earned her a second consecutive UK No. 1 album — a remarkably fast turnaround for a full-length follow-up. She teased the announcement at her headline show at London's O2 Arena on Wednesday night, with audio of meows playing over the sound system as the lights came up, and previewed 'No Punctuation' in the encore. The new record was written and recorded at home in her East London living room with her friend Luca and her two cats, she says, and its 14 songs are the softer foil to 'Pylon's harder rock sound — the two records representing different sides of the same person. 'No Punctuation' itself dates back more than four years, with early versions previously circulating online. Her Powerlines tour resumes in Europe next week before dates in Australia, New Zealand and Asia in 2027.

articles.title: ENHYPEN drop new single 'I Want You' to close out The Sin series
articles.description: ENHYPEN have released a new single, 'I Want You,' out today, November 19. The romantic track closes out the K-pop group's The Sin album series, which has kept them on the Billboard 200 for months.
articles.body: ENHYPEN have released a new single, 'I Want You,' out today, November 19, closing out the K-pop group's The Sin album series. The romantic track marks the end of a series that has kept the group on the Billboard charts for months — their album 'Romance: Untold' became their first to spend 15 weeks on the Billboard 200. ENHYPEN, who debuted in 2020, have built one of the most consistent chart runs in K-pop's current generation, and the new single is positioned as a bridge to their next era, with the group announcing three comebacks in a single year. The release comes as K-pop continues to dominate Billboard's charts, with multiple Korean acts holding top positions at once, from Jennie's 'Dracula' on the Hot 100 to P1Harmony's Billboard 200 debut. 'I Want You' is available on streaming services now.

articles.title: Future's 'Ya Hit' with Drake, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy enters the Hot 100 at No. 38
articles.description: Future's 'Ya Hit,' featuring Drake, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy, enters the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 38 on the chart dated November 21. Drake also holds two more entries on the same chart — 'Solar Eclipse' with Don Toliver at No. 56 and 'Cold Shoulder' at No. 62.
articles.body: Future's 'Ya Hit,' featuring Drake, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy, enters the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 38 on the chart dated November 21, 2026. The track is a new entry on the main US singles chart, credited to Future featuring Drake, Travis Scott and Loe Shimmy, with production by ATL Jacob and released on the Sahluna/Epic imprint. The entry extends Drake's 2026 run of Hot 100 collaborations: the same November 21 chart lists 'Solar Eclipse' at No. 56, credited to Drake and Don Toliver, and 'Cold Shoulder' at No. 62, credited to Drake, Don Toliver and Yebba. For Future, the debut adds another Hot 100 entry to a catalogue that has made him one of the chart's most consistent presences, and the four-way collaboration — pairing three of rap's biggest names with rising artist Loe Shimmy — is one of the week's most high-profile chart arrivals.

articles.title: Drake's 'Views' hits 520 weeks on the Billboard 200 — a full decade on the chart
articles.description: Drake's 'Views' has reached 520 weeks on the Billboard 200 — a full decade on the albums chart — climbing from No. 43 to No. 36 this week. It is his third album to celebrate ten years on the tally, after 'Take Care' (687 weeks) and 'Nothing Was The Same' (522 weeks).
articles.body: Drake's 'Views' has reached 520 weeks on the Billboard 200 — a full decade as one of the 200 most-consumed albums in the United States. The album climbs back into the top 40 this week, jumping from No. 43 to No. 36, and it currently ranks as Drake's second-highest-placing set, behind only 'Take Care.' 'Views' is his third project to celebrate an entire decade on the Billboard 200: just two weeks ago, 'Nothing Was The Same' became his second, and it is now up to 522 weeks on the roster, while 'Take Care' holds as his longest-charting album with 687 weeks to its credit. The album, which includes his longest-running No. 1 on the chart, is one of his 14 Billboard 200 No. 1s. This week 'Views' appears on four Billboard charts, and it is a top-10 hit on half of them. Drake's 'Her Loss' with 21 Savage also re-enters the Billboard 200 at No. 191, underlining the staying power of his catalogue a decade after 'Views' first topped the chart.

articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin open first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen
articles.description: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have opened the first-ever trilateral summit of the US, Russian and Chinese leaders, meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen. The talks began at 9:30 AM Moscow time, with the war in Ukraine, nuclear weapons and Iran on the agenda. After opening statements, the leaders continued behind closed doors.
articles.body: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have opened the first-ever trilateral summit of the leaders of the United States, Russia and China, meeting in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit. The session began at 9:30 AM Moscow time, and Meduza is covering it live. Xi devoted his opening remarks to nuclear weapons, saying they should be completely banned and destroyed. Trump said it was necessary to protect the sovereignty of nations from 'out-of-control globalist organisations' and that ending Russia's war against Ukraine would be one of the main topics. Putin said the three countries shared an interest in 'settling regional conflicts, including in Ukraine', and noted the issue had already come up in his meetings with Xi on November 18 and with Trump earlier in the day. After the opening statements, the talks continued behind closed doors. No breakthrough is expected: Trump has said the leaders might also discuss nuclear arms control and Iran, while allies in Europe — pointedly not invited — watch from Berlin, where the Coalition of the Willing meets the same day.

articles.title: Crimean Bridge hit a third time this week as leaders meet in Shenzhen
articles.description: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge for the third time this week early on Thursday, halting rail traffic between Russia and occupied Crimea just days after a road span collapsed into the sea. The strike landed as Putin was about to meet Trump and Xi in Shenzhen. Russia confirmed the attack but has not disclosed the scale of the damage.
articles.body: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge — Vladimir Putin's prized link to occupied Crimea — for the third time this week early on Thursday, halting rail traffic between Russia and the peninsula just days after a section of the road bridge collapsed into the sea. The timing was pointed: the attack came as Putin was meeting Trump on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, ahead of the historic trilateral talks with Xi. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov was quoted by the Russian state news agency TASS as saying Putin came out of his meeting with Trump in an 'excellent mood', adding that Ukraine was the main topic of discussion. Before the meeting, Trump praised his 'great relationship' with Putin, calling him 'my friend'. Meduza reports the overnight strike targeted the bridge's railway section, which had survived the earlier attacks, and says Ukraine used Neptune missiles; the exact weapon and the extent of the new damage remain unclear. Meanwhile in Berlin, the Coalition of the Willing — Ukraine's key allies — was expected to convene on Thursday with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in attendance.

articles.title: GTA VI is out worldwide — 99 on Metacritic and over $1.65 billion already banked
articles.description: Rockstar Games has released Grand Theft Auto VI globally on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, thirteen years after GTA V. The game holds a 99 on Metacritic, tying The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated game ever, and analysts say it has already sold more than 17 million copies for over $1.65 billion. No PC release date has been announced.
articles.body: Rockstar Games has released Grand Theft Auto VI globally, and the game is now available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The launch caps a thirteen-year wait since GTA V and one of the most anticipated releases in the history of the medium. Set in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida, with Vice City at its centre, the game follows two protagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. Critics have been unanimous: the game holds 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, tying The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated game of all time, and 98 on OpenCritic, where 100% of reviewers recommend it. The commercial numbers are just as striking — Sensor Tower estimates more than 17 million copies sold before launch day, worth over $1.65 billion, and Take-Two's shares closed 6.2% higher on Wednesday. Players who pre-ordered got a day-one patch to install, and the game unlocked at midnight in each region, starting in New Zealand. A PC version is expected eventually, but Rockstar has still not given a date for it.

articles.title: Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin today, with Witkoff and Kushner at the table
articles.description: The Coalition of the Willing — more than 30 allied leaders — meets in Berlin today to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine, with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner attending. President Zelenskyy called the meeting important and said Ukraine is preparing new support packages for its defence and energy sector. The session is chaired by Germany's Friedrich Merz, France's Emmanuel Macron and Britain's Andy Burnham.
articles.body: The Coalition of the Willing, the group of Ukraine's key allies, convenes in Berlin today, November 19, with more than 30 leaders expected. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet Ukrainian officials and the European negotiating group on the sidelines, with reliable post-war security guarantees for Kyiv, a comprehensive economic recovery plan and preparations for the next round of multilateral talks on the agenda. The meeting will be chaired by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham. In his evening address on November 18, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the meeting important and said Ukraine is preparing new support packages — 'for our defence first of all, for our energy' — and that bilateral meetings on the margins 'should give more to Ukraine and to our diplomacy'. The Berlin talks run in parallel with the Trump–Putin–Xi summit in Shenzhen, where the war is also on the agenda, but Europe has no seat at that table.

articles.title: Warner Music chief Robert Kyncl to keynote CES 2027 — a first for a music-industry leader
articles.description: Warner Music Group CEO Robert Kyncl will deliver a keynote at CES 2027 in Las Vegas on January 6, the Consumer Technology Association has announced. He will be the first music-industry leader ever to keynote the tech show. WMG is the only major label to have settled its copyright lawsuit with Suno, striking a licensing deal with the AI music platform in November 2025.
articles.body: Warner Music Group CEO Robert Kyncl will deliver a keynote address at CES 2027 in Las Vegas, the Consumer Technology Association announced on Wednesday, November 18. According to the CTA, the session will make Kyncl 'the first music-industry leader to keynote the world's most powerful tech event'. He is scheduled to take the stage on January 6 at 2 PM PT in the Palazzo Ballroom at the Venetian, on the first day of the show, which runs until January 9. The booking is a sign of how central music — and AI music in particular — has become to the tech industry's agenda: WMG is the only major label to have settled its copyright lawsuit against the AI music platform Suno, striking a licensing partnership in November 2025, while Universal and Sony are still fighting Suno in court. The CTA also highlighted WMG's inclusion on TIME's 2026 TIME100 Most Influential Companies list. WMG's fiscal 2027 began on October 1, 2026.

articles.title: CMA Awards 2026: Taylor Swift honours Brooks & Dunn as Ella Langley takes Album of the Year
articles.description: The 2026 CMA Awards delivered a night of throwbacks and tributes: Taylor Swift honoured Brooks & Dunn and threw it back with 'Our Song', Ella Langley's 'Dandelion' was named Album of the Year, and Halestorm, Brothers Osborne and Hardy led a ferocious tribute to the country duo. Miranda Lambert and Ella Langley gave the live debut of 'Snakeskin Boots', and Stephen Wilson Jr. performed 'I'm a Song' with Chris Stapleton.
articles.body: The 2026 CMA Awards, held on Wednesday night, turned into a celebration of country music's past and present. Taylor Swift took the stage to honour Brooks & Dunn, calling them 'eternal bangers', and threw it back with a performance of her early hit 'Our Song'. Ella Langley — already the biggest chart story of the year with a record 28 weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100 — won Album of the Year for 'Dandelion', and she and Miranda Lambert gave the live debut of their duet 'Snakeskin Boots'. The night's most ferocious moment was the tribute to Brooks & Dunn, with Halestorm, Brothers Osborne, Hardy, Marcus King and Luke Bryan backing the duo's songs. Stephen Wilson Jr. and Chris Stapleton performed their collaboration 'I'm a Song', and Lainey Wilson debuted a new song with an all-female band. Rolling Stone has the complete winners list from the night.

articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack sets a 67-week No. 1 record
articles.description: The 'KPop Demon Hunters' soundtrack has made Billboard chart history, becoming the soundtrack with the most weeks at No. 1 on the Top Soundtracks chart — 67 weeks, passing the previous record of 62 held by Disney's 'Moana'. Its hit 'Golden', performed by the fictional group HUNTR/X, also spent eight nonconsecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100.
articles.body: The 'KPop Demon Hunters' soundtrack has made Billboard chart history, becoming the soundtrack with the most weeks at No. 1 on the Top Soundtracks chart. According to Billboard's November 3 chart update, the soundtrack from Netflix's animated film has spent 67 weeks in the top position, surpassing the previous record of 62 weeks held by Disney's 'Moana'. Billboard launched the Top Soundtracks chart in June 2001 to track albums connected to movies, television and other screen properties, so the record spans nearly a quarter-century of soundtracks. The soundtrack's success extends beyond the album chart: its hit song 'Golden', performed by the fictional K-pop group HUNTR/X, also reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, spending eight nonconsecutive weeks at the top. The film's music has become one of the defining pop stories of the year, with the fictional group functioning as a real chart act.

articles.title: Are we in 'the jackpot'? CNN on the cascade of tech outages
articles.description: After a week in which the Microsoft outage, an FAA nationwide ground stop, and glitches at Workday, Chase, United Airlines, the NSA's internal network and Apple all piled up, CNN asks whether we are living through 'the jackpot' — William Gibson's term for a slow, cascading collapse. Experts say the failures expose how dependent the world is on a handful of Silicon Valley companies.
articles.body: One crucial computer system after another failed in the past week — the global Microsoft outage, followed by the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop, followed by more outages and glitches hitting Workday, Chase Bank, United Airlines, the National Security Agency's internal communications system and Apple — and CNN asks whether we are living through 'the jackpot'. The term comes from the science-fiction novelist William Gibson, who coined it in his 2014 novel 'The Peripheral' for a slow-moving cascade of crises: climate breakdown, economic instability and institutional failure arriving not as one apocalypse but as a pile-up. The piece notes it is not just the tech failures: this week the US also lost its measles elimination status, parts of Florida were hit with severe flooding after more than a foot of rain, and the summer just past was the hottest on record. Existential-risk researcher Luke Kemp says the Microsoft Outlook outage disrupting basic operations across so many institutions is a sign of the world's critical dependence on a handful of corporations in Silicon Valley — and of the erosion of national sovereignty that follows. Astrophysicist Daniel Holz, who chairs the Science and Security Board behind the Doomsday Clock, notes the clock now stands at 85 seconds to midnight, the closest since it was created in 1947.

articles.title: Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen — the first trilateral summit of its kind
articles.description: Meduza is running a live blog of the 1,730th day of the war as Trump, Putin and Xi meet in Shenzhen. The session began at 9:30 AM Moscow time; Xi devoted his opening remarks to nuclear weapons, Trump spoke of protecting sovereignty from 'out-of-control globalist organisations', and Putin said settling regional conflicts, including in Ukraine, was a shared interest. Talks then continued behind closed doors.
articles.body: Meduza is covering the 1,730th day of the war with a live blog centred on the meeting of Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. The trilateral session — the first of its kind — began at 9:30 AM Moscow time on the sidelines of the APEC summit. Xi devoted his opening remarks to nuclear weapons, saying they should be completely banned and destroyed. Trump said in his opening statement that it was necessary to protect the sovereignty of nations from 'out-of-control globalist organisations', and that ending Russia's war against Ukraine would still be one of the main topics. Putin said one of the common themes for the three countries was 'the settlement of regional conflicts, including in Ukraine', and noted the issue had been discussed at his meeting with Xi the day before and in his talks with Trump that morning. He also said Russia, the US and China were united not only by their status as victors in the Second World War but by responsibility for maintaining international peace. After the leaders made their statements, the negotiations continued behind closed doors.

articles.title: Ukraine attacks the Crimean Bridge overnight — the third strike in a week
articles.description: Overnight into November 19, Ukraine attacked the Crimean Bridge again, this time targeting its railway section, which had survived the earlier attacks. It is the third attack on the bridge in a week, and it came hours before Putin was due to meet Trump and Xi. Rail traffic has been halted; the extent of the new damage is unclear.
articles.body: Overnight into November 19, Ukraine attacked the Crimean Bridge again, targeting its railway section, which had survived the earlier attacks this week. This is the third attack on the bridge in a week, following the strikes on November 16 and 17 that sent a road arch crashing into the sea. Meduza reports that Ukraine used Neptune missiles, and that the Russian-installed head of Crimea, Sergey Aksyonov, confirmed the attack and the suspension of rail traffic, saying there were no casualties. The exact weapon used and the scale of the new damage remain unclear. The strike landed on the morning that Vladimir Putin was scheduled to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, and it is the latest in a campaign that has turned the bridge — Putin's prestige project and a key military supply route — into a recurring target. Ukrainian forces say the road section is 'dead' and no car will pass on it.

articles.title: Four ways China treated Trump and Putin differently at the APEC summit
articles.description: Meduza compares the receptions China gave the two leaders in Shenzhen: Trump landed to an 'unprecedented' airport greeting from Xi himself, while Putin's arrival drew noticeably cooler treatment, with multiple signs that Beijing kept him at arm's length. The contrast sets the tone for the trilateral meeting.
articles.body: Meduza looks at how China treated Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin differently as the APEC summit opened in Shenzhen on November 18. Trump landed to what his team called an 'unprecedented' airport greeting, with Xi Jinping himself there to meet him — a rare honour. Putin's arrival, by contrast, drew noticeably cooler treatment, and by the eve of the summit there were multiple signs that Beijing was keeping the Russian leader at arm's length. The piece catalogues four contrasts in protocol, staging and public messaging between the two visits. The choreography matters because the trilateral meeting is Xi's show: China is hosting, and the seating, the greetings and the photo opportunities all signal where Beijing thinks the leverage lies. For Putin, who arrived hoping to present himself as an equal partner in a new great-power triangle, the cool reception was a pointed reminder of who is setting the terms.

articles.title: US warns Russia to make peace with Ukraine now, while Trump still has room to negotiate
articles.description: The United States has warned Russia that it should make peace with Ukraine now, while President Trump still has room to negotiate, The Kyiv Independent reports via Meduza. The warning comes as the trilateral summit opens in Shenzhen and the Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin.
articles.body: The United States has warned Russia that it should make peace with Ukraine now, while President Trump still has room to negotiate, The Kyiv Independent reports, as cited by Meduza. The message is aimed at Moscow on the day the three leaders meet in Shenzhen: Washington's argument is that Trump's political space to broker a deal is not unlimited, and that delay risks a harder American line. It is the latest signal that the US administration is pressing both sides toward a settlement — Witkoff and Kushner are in Berlin the same day talking to Ukrainian and European officials about post-war security guarantees — while keeping the pressure on Russia to come to the table. The warning also carries an implicit threat: if Moscow drags the war out, the terms on offer now may not be the terms on offer later.

articles.title: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut Russian oil refining by 45% since late October, Reuters reports
articles.description: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut the amount of oil Russia refines by 45% since late October, according to estimates two industry sources shared with Reuters. The strikes have disrupted or halted operations at 15 of Russia's 35 largest refineries, and some regions have reinstated restrictions on gasoline sales.
articles.body: Ukrainian drone attacks have cut the amount of oil Russian refineries process by 45% since late October, according to estimates two industry sources shared with Reuters, as reported by Meduza. The attacks have disrupted or halted operations at 15 of Russia's 35 largest refineries, turning the long-range drone campaign into one of the war's most effective economic weapons. As the strikes intensified in early November, some Russian regions began reinstating restrictions on gasoline sales at filling stations, and Moscow has sharply increased gasoline imports to cover the shortfall — seaborne imports hit a record 390,000 tonnes in October, while domestic production is estimated to cover only 60–65% of demand. The campaign's logic is straightforward: refineries are harder to repair than to hit, and every week of reduced output tightens fuel supplies for both the civilian economy and the military. Russia has not published official figures on the damage.

articles.title: Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge with Ruta missiles from a Swiss firm founded by a Russian-born entrepreneur
articles.description: Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge with Ruta cruise missiles made by a company founded in Switzerland by Russian-born Mikhail Kokorich, after the US barred him from his own startup's technology. The missiles are the latest addition to Ukraine's growing arsenal of long-range weapons built outside the usual defence-industry channels.
articles.body: Ukraine hit the Crimean Bridge with Ruta cruise missiles produced by a firm founded in Switzerland by Russian-born entrepreneur Mikhail Kokorich, Meduza reports. Kokorich built the company after the United States barred him from his own startup's technology — a backstory that captures how much of Ukraine's long-range strike capability now comes from unconventional, fast-moving suppliers rather than traditional defence giants. The Ruta missile is part of a broadening Ukrainian arsenal that also includes the Neptune and Flamingo missiles Zelenskyy has credited with the bridge strikes. The point of the campaign is cumulative: each strike on the bridge degrades a symbol of Russian control over Crimea and a supply route for the occupation, while demonstrating that Kyiv can keep reaching deep into Russian-held territory.

articles.title: Russia's demands for ending the war are clarifying — NATO back to 1997, and concessions in Kaliningrad
articles.description: New details of Russia's negotiating demands have emerged via The New York Times and Bloomberg, as reported by Meduza: Moscow wants the EU and NATO to return to the borders of 1997 and stop calling Russia an 'adversary or threat'. In exchange, Russia is reportedly ready to reduce its military presence in Kaliningrad and Belarus.
articles.body: New details of Russia's demands and offers in the peace talks have emerged from reporting by The New York Times and Bloomberg, summarised by Meduza in its war live blog. In negotiations in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11, the Russian side demanded that the European Union and NATO not only return to the borders of 1997 but also stop considering Moscow an 'adversary or threat' — effectively a demand to rewrite Europe's post-Cold War security architecture. In exchange, Bloomberg's sources say, Russia is prepared to reduce its military presence in Kaliningrad and Belarus if its demands are met. US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are said to believe that if Russia and Europe can agree on a post-war 'security architecture' for the continent, it could help end the war. The two men meet Ukrainian and European officials in Berlin on November 19 to discuss security guarantees for Kyiv. The demands are maximalist, and it is far from clear that Europe would accept them — but the fact that Moscow is now putting concrete offers on the table, rather than just ultimatums, is itself a development.

articles.title: "The train goes no further": Crimean Bridge railway damaged by Neptune missiles
articles.description: The railway section of the Crimean Bridge was damaged by Neptune missiles in the overnight strike into November 19, Ukrainska Pravda reports — 'the train goes no further'. It is the third attack on the bridge in three days, and rail traffic across the crossing has been suspended. Russia confirmed the attack but has not disclosed the scale of the damage.
articles.body: The railway section of the Crimean Bridge was damaged by Neptune missiles in the overnight strike into November 19, Ukrainska Pravda reports under the headline 'The train goes no further'. It is the third attack on the bridge in three days, after the strikes on November 16 and 17 that collapsed a road span, and this time the target was the railway — the part of the crossing that had kept functioning. Rail traffic across the bridge has been suspended. The Russian-installed authorities in Crimea confirmed the attack and the halt to trains but did not disclose the scale of the damage, and said there were no casualties. The strike came hours before Putin's meeting with Trump and Xi in Shenzhen, and it is the latest in a campaign that has turned the bridge — Putin's prestige project and a key military supply route — into a recurring target. The SBU says the bridge's road section is 'dead' and no car will pass on it; now the rail link is damaged too.

articles.title: Trump and Putin to meet in China; Zelenskyy: Russia doesn't want a truce, only Ukraine's capitulation
articles.description: As Trump and Putin meet in Shenzhen, President Zelenskyy says Russia does not want a truce and seeks only Ukraine's capitulation. The warning frames Kyiv's position on the day the three leaders sit down together — and on the day the Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin without a seat at the Shenzhen table.
articles.body: As Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin meet in Shenzhen, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Russia does not want a truce and seeks only Ukraine's capitulation. The statement, carried as one of Ukrainska Pravda's lead stories on November 19, frames Kyiv's position on the day the three leaders sit down together: from Ukraine's point of view, Moscow is not negotiating toward a settlement but toward surrender. The warning lands as the trilateral summit opens with the war on its agenda and as the Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin to discuss security guarantees for Kyiv — with Europe pointedly absent from the Shenzhen table. Zelenskyy has repeatedly said air defence is Ukraine's top priority and that partners must supply interceptor missiles, and the Berlin meeting is expected to produce new support packages for Ukraine's defence and energy sector.

articles.title: Kushner and Witkoff to go to Berlin to discuss security guarantees with the Coalition of the Willing
articles.description: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Berlin to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine with the Coalition of the Willing. The meeting, chaired by Germany's Friedrich Merz, France's Emmanuel Macron and Britain's Andy Burnham, will also cover economic recovery and the next round of multilateral talks.
articles.body: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Berlin to discuss security guarantees for Ukraine with the Coalition of the Willing, Ukrainska Pravda reports. The meeting of more than 30 allied leaders takes place today, November 19, and the agenda covers reliable post-war security guarantees for Kyiv, a comprehensive economic recovery plan and preparations for the next round of multilateral talks. The session will be chaired by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham. In his evening address on November 18, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the meeting important and said Ukraine is preparing new support packages — 'for our defence first of all, for our energy' — and that bilateral meetings on the margins 'should give more to Ukraine and to our diplomacy'. The Berlin talks run in parallel with the Trump–Putin–Xi summit in Shenzhen, where the war is also on the agenda, but without Europe at the table.

articles.title: "Second time this week": Zelenskyy confirms the Crimean Bridge was hit a third time
articles.description: President Zelenskyy has confirmed that the Crimean Bridge was struck a third time, Ukrainska Pravda reports. The overnight strike targeted the bridge's railway section, which had survived the earlier attacks, and rail traffic has been halted.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has confirmed that the Crimean Bridge was struck a third time, Ukrainska Pravda reports. The overnight strike into November 19 targeted the bridge's railway section, which had survived the attacks of November 16 and 17 that collapsed a road span. Zelenskyy's confirmation follows the earlier Ukrainian claims that the bridge was hit with Neptune missiles and that its road section is 'dead'. The Russian-installed authorities in Crimea confirmed the attack and the suspension of rail services but did not disclose the scale of the damage. The strike came hours before Putin's meeting with Trump and Xi in Shenzhen, and it is the latest in a campaign that has made the bridge — the road and rail link between Russia and occupied Crimea — a recurring target.

articles.title: Zelenskyy explains why Ukraine needs to destroy the Crimean Bridge
articles.description: President Zelenskyy has explained why Ukraine needs to destroy the Crimean Bridge, Ukrainska Pravda reports. The bridge is both a symbol of Russian control over Crimea and a working military supply route — and each strike degrades both.
articles.body: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has explained why Ukraine needs to destroy the Crimean Bridge, Ukrainska Pravda reports. The bridge is both a symbol of Russian control over Crimea and a working military supply route, and the campaign against it serves both purposes at once: each strike degrades the occupation's logistics and demonstrates that Kyiv can keep reaching deep into Russian-held territory. The road section is already, in the SBU's words, 'dead' — no car will pass on it — and the overnight strike into November 19 damaged the railway section that had kept functioning. Zelenskyy's explanation comes as the bridge is hit for the third time in a week, hours before Putin meets Trump and Xi in Shenzhen.

articles.title: Holiday in Vice City: GTA VI is out worldwide
articles.description: Rockstar Games has announced the global release of Grand Theft Auto VI, now available on Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5. The game is set in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida, and holds a 99 on Metacritic. A PC release is expected eventually, but Rockstar has not given a date.
articles.body: Rockstar Games has announced the global release of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is now available on Xbox Series X|S and PlayStation 5, unlocking at midnight in each region, starting in New Zealand. The action takes place in the fictional American state of Leonida, inspired by real-life Florida, with Vice City at its centre. Critics have been unanimous: the game holds 99 out of 100 on Metacritic, tying The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and 98 on OpenCritic. It is the highest-rated game of 2026 and of the current console generation. A PC release is expected in due course, but Rockstar has not disclosed the timing of the port. Players are already digging into the game — and finding its secrets, including Bigfoot in the forests of Leonida.

articles.title: No punishments for improvising: GTA VI reworks its mission system
articles.description: Rockstar has completely reworked how missions work in GTA VI, removing the artificial barriers between free exploration and mission objectives. Players can go off-script and choose their own way to reach a goal without the game flashing 'mission failed'. Design VP Stephen Donkin confirmed the change in an interview.
articles.body: Rockstar Games has completely reworked the structure of missions in GTA VI, cutting the artificial boundaries between free exploration of the world and completing objectives. The new engine code is designed for non-linear play: players can step away from the script and choose their own way of reaching a goal without the game telling them they have failed. Design vice-president Stephen Donkin confirmed the changes in an interview, noting the team built smooth transitions between different kinds of activity. Technology VP David Hynd explained that the developers have adopted a different design philosophy for the game. The system will now far more rarely report a mission failure — a change that should make the open world feel genuinely open rather than a series of corridors with a fail state at the end of each one.

articles.title: Players already found Bigfoot in GTA VI — Rockstar revives the series' legendary mystery
articles.description: Hours after launch, players have already found Bigfoot in the forests of Leonida. Several players posted videos of the creature in the same spot, at a dirt-road crossing where it is eating a deer carcass — and chasing it leads to a strange structure in the woods. Rockstar has not commented on the find.
articles.body: Grand Theft Auto VI has only just come out, and players are already uncovering its secrets. One of the first finds is Bigfoot, the legendary creature whose rumours have followed the series for more than 20 years, since GTA: San Andreas in 2004. Several players have posted videos of an encounter with the creature, all in roughly the same place: at the crossing of dirt roads in the forests of Leonida, where Bigfoot is eating a deer carcass. If you chase it, it leads the player to a strange structure in the forest. It is not yet known whether the encounter is a one-off Easter egg or the start of a larger mystery, and Rockstar has not officially commented on the find. Either way, it is a deliberate nod to one of the series' longest-running legends.

articles.title: Free up your SSD: Rare cuts the Sea of Thieves client by 50%
articles.description: Rare is releasing a big Sea of Thieves update today, November 19, that cuts the game's client size by about 50% on all platforms — down to 53.2 GB on Steam and 28.3 GB on Xbox One. The studio cleaned out unused resources accumulated over years of live-service updates.
articles.body: Rare has announced that on November 19 it will release a major update for Sea of Thieves aimed at solving a key problem for long-running live-service games: the client ballooning in size as new content piles up. After clearing out unused resources, the Sea of Thieves client has shrunk by an average of 50% on all available platforms. On Steam the game will weigh 53.2 GB after the update, and the Xbox One version just 28.3 GB. The timing is pointed: the slimmed-down update lands on the same day as the global release of GTA VI, after which companies like EA were publicly begging players on social media not to delete their games to make room. Rare, meanwhile, simply freed up space on players' hard drives. The studio has also recently moved under the Activision Blizzard wing.

articles.title: Russian console sales flat in 2026 — GTA VI is the only thing holding the market up
articles.description: Analytical firm ICMR, via retailer M.Video, reports that about 1.05 million consoles were sold in Russia in the first nine months of 2026 — roughly the same as a year earlier, after growth of 8% a year since 2022. Without GTA VI's release on November 19, experts say sales could have fallen 5%. Distributor OCS expects 2026 sales 5–10% below 2025.
articles.body: Analytical company ICMR has analysed console sales in Russia for 2026 and concluded they have stayed at roughly the same level. M.Video shared the data with specialists: in the first nine months of the year, about 1.05 million consoles were sold in the country — as many as in the same period of 2025. That flatline follows growth of 8% a year since 2022, and experts say that without the release of Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, sales could have fallen by 5%. Distributor OCS also notes declining demand, estimating that 2026 sales could end up 5–10% lower than in 2025. The figures show how much of the console market now rides on a single release: in a year with no new hardware, one game is doing the work of an entire product cycle.

articles.title: GTA VI: The Album reportedly slips a day to November 20
articles.description: The 34-track 'GTA VI: The Album', made with Atlantic Records, is reportedly moving from November 19 to November 20, one day after the game launches. The claim comes from the news account Daily Noud, and Apple Music's pre-release page now lists November 20 — but Rockstar has not announced any change and its own music page still says November 19.
articles.body: The 34-track soundtrack 'GTA VI: The Album', which Rockstar Games is releasing with Atlantic Records, is reportedly moving from November 19 to November 20, one day after the game launches. The news account Daily Noud posted the claim on November 11, and an Apple Music pre-release page for the album now lists November 20 as its release date. Rockstar has not announced a change, and its own music page still gives November 19 for the album. There is a practical reason a one-day slip would make sense: November 19 is a Thursday and November 20 is a Friday, and Billboard's tracking week runs Friday through Thursday — a Thursday release would split first-week activity across two tracking weeks, while a Friday release keeps it all in one. For now, though, the delay is unconfirmed, and fans should watch Rockstar's newswire and the album's streaming pages for the date to settle.

articles.title: Russia and China are not America's friends. Why does Trump think they are?
articles.description: CNN's analysis of the Shenzhen summit argues the symbolism is stark: three great powers, each claiming hegemony in its own orbit, sending a signal of dominance that deliberately excludes smaller, weaker nations. Breakthroughs are not expected — Trump says the leaders might discuss nuclear weapons, Iran and Ukraine — but the meeting tests the line between useful diplomacy and strongman role-play.
articles.body: CNN's analysis of the trilateral summit argues the symbolism of the Shenzhen meeting is stark: three great powers, each staking a hegemonic claim in its wider geographical orbit, sending a signal of dominance that deliberately excludes smaller, weaker nations. Trump hopes to complete a trifecta of strongman check-ins by also meeting North Korea's Kim Jong Un. The piece notes the jarring dynamic of an American president who seems to regard Putin and Xi as friends may re-emerge in full: former US ambassador to China Nicholas Burns asked on CNN what the US actually gains from arms-control talks with the two leaders, and Trump's first-term vice-president Mike Pence told CNN the president should take a firm stance. Trump, Putin and Xi met late on Wednesday at a welcome banquet for the APEC summit on the eve of their trilateral meeting. Retired Admiral James Stavridis told CNN the summit may test the boundaries between useful diplomacy to lower superpower tensions and dictator role-play between two strongmen and an American president who would like to be one. Breakthroughs are not expected in Shenzhen: Trump says the leaders might discuss nuclear weapons, Iran and Ukraine.

articles.title: Putin's prized bridge to occupied Crimea has been hit for the third time this week
articles.description: Russia's Kerch Bridge was struck for the third time this week early on Thursday, halting rail traffic between Russia and occupied Crimea just days after a section of the road bridge collapsed. The attack came as Putin was meeting Trump in Shenzhen ahead of the trilateral talks with Xi.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin's prized Kerch Bridge was struck for the third time this week early on Thursday, halting rail traffic between Russia and occupied Crimea just days after a section of the road bridge collapsed. The third strike came at a significant moment, as Putin was about to meet US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Asia. The latest attack on the bridge came as Putin was meeting Trump on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, ahead of their historic trilateral talks with Xi. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov was quoted by Russian state news agency TASS as saying the Russian leader came out of the meeting in an 'excellent mood', adding that Ukraine was the main topic of discussion. Before the meeting, Trump praised his 'great relationship' with Putin, calling him 'my friend'. Trump has renewed his push for a negotiated end to Russia's war on Ukraine in recent months. Meanwhile in Berlin, the Coalition of the Willing was expected to convene on Thursday with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in attendance.

articles.title: What is 'the jackpot'? Are we in it? Will we die?
articles.description: After a week of cascading failures — the Microsoft outage, the FAA's nationwide ground stop, glitches at Workday, Chase, United, the NSA and Apple — CNN explains 'the jackpot', William Gibson's term from his 2014 novel 'The Peripheral' for a slow pile-up of crises. Experts say the outages expose dependence on a handful of Silicon Valley firms.
articles.body: As one crucial computer system after another failed in the past week — triggering the global Microsoft outage, followed by the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop, followed by more outages and glitches hitting Workday, Chase Bank, United Airlines, the National Security Agency's internal communications system and Apple — many people asked whether this was a string of cyberattacks, or the result of pushing too much AI too fast. CNN's Word of the Week turns to 'the jackpot', a term coined by the science-fiction novelist William Gibson in his 2014 novel 'The Peripheral': a slow-moving cascade of crises — climate breakdown, economic instability, institutional failure — arriving not as one apocalypse but as a pile-up. It is not just the tech failures, the piece notes: this week the US also lost its measles elimination status, parts of Florida were hit with severe flooding after more than a foot of rain, and the summer just past was the hottest on record, marked by drought, wildfires and Britain's worst cereal harvest in four decades. Existential-risk researcher Luke Kemp says the Microsoft Outlook outage disrupting basic operations across so many institutions is a sign of the world's critical dependence on a handful of corporations in Silicon Valley. Astrophysicist Daniel Holz, who chairs the Science and Security Board behind the Doomsday Clock, notes the clock stands at 85 seconds to midnight — the closest since its inception in 1947.

articles.title: UN's top court orders Myanmar to stop genocide of Rohingya and allow their return
articles.description: The International Court of Justice has ordered Myanmar to stop the genocide of the Rohingya and allow the displaced minority to return home. The ruling is the latest step in a case over the military's 2017 crackdown, which drove hundreds of thousands of Rohingya into Bangladesh.
articles.body: The International Court of Justice, the UN's top court, has ordered Myanmar to stop the genocide of the Rohingya and allow the displaced minority to return home. The ruling is the latest step in a case brought over the military's 2017 crackdown in Rakhine State, which drove hundreds of thousands of Rohingya into neighbouring Bangladesh, where most still live in refugee camps. The court's order is legally binding, though the ICJ has no enforcement mechanism of its own — compliance depends on political pressure from the UN and member states. Myanmar's military government, which seized power in 2021, has denied that a genocide took place. The ruling keeps one of the world's most protracted refugee crises on the international agenda at a moment when attention is focused elsewhere.

articles.title: Analysis: the trilateral talks already handed China a major win
articles.description: CNN's analysis argues the trilateral summit has already handed China a major win before it even began: Xi is hosting, setting the terms, and presenting China as the indispensable power — while Trump and Putin come to Shenzhen as guests. The staging, not the substance, is the story.
articles.body: CNN's analysis argues the trilateral talks have already handed China a major win — before the leaders even sat down. Xi Jinping is the host, and that matters: China set the venue, the choreography and the terms of the meeting, presenting itself as the indispensable power while Trump and Putin arrive in Shenzhen as guests. The piece notes the contrast with the cooler treatment Putin received on arrival, compared with the 'unprecedented' airport greeting for Trump, and argues that the staging itself is the message. For Beijing, the summit is a chance to show that the world's most important conversations now happen on Chinese terms. For Washington, the risk is that the symbolism of the three-way meeting — three great powers deciding the fate of smaller nations between them — does the work of legitimising a carve-up, whatever the communique says.

articles.title: Amazon's annual Black Friday sale is officially live with 12 days of deals
articles.description: Amazon's annual Black Friday sale is officially live, running for 12 days with what CNN Underscored calls some of the best discounts of the year on nearly everything the retailer sells. Prices have already fallen to their official Black Friday levels, meaning the deals won't get better next week or on Cyber Monday.
articles.body: Amazon's annual Black Friday sale is officially live. For the next 12 days, the retailer will be offering some of the best discounts of the year on nearly everything it sells, according to CNN Underscored's deals editors. Just about everything on offer has already fallen to its official Black Friday price, meaning the deals won't get better next week or even into Cyber Monday — the price you see now is the price. The sale covers electronics in particular, with Black Friday pricing already live on Apple's newest flagship smartwatch — $70 off — and on Apple's newest Bluetooth trackers. CNN Underscored's deals editors cross-reference their colleagues' tested gear to find the discounts worth acting on, and they note that the early start is now the norm: the 'Black Friday' window has stretched from a single day into nearly two weeks of deals.

articles.title: New video of NYC building collapse, filmed from a bus
articles.description: CNN has new video of a building collapse in New York City, filmed from a bus as the structure came down. The footage is the latest look at the collapse, which happened in Brooklyn.
articles.body: CNN has obtained new video of a building collapse in New York City, filmed from a passing bus as the structure came down. The footage shows the collapse from street level, from the perspective of passengers on the bus. The video is the latest look at the incident in Brooklyn, and it captures the moment the building gave way in real time. Details of injuries and the cause of the collapse are still emerging.

articles.title: Carlyle-backed Litmus Music secures $475M in new capital, with KKR joining as an investor
articles.description: Litmus Music has secured approximately $475 million in new capital commitments from Carlyle and funds managed by KKR, which joins as a new investor. Carlyle Global Credit, which founded Litmus in 2022 with Hank Forsyth and Dan McCarroll, keeps its majority stake. Litmus now has about $1.4 billion in assets under management.
articles.body: Litmus Music has secured approximately $475 million in new capital commitments from Carlyle and funds managed by KKR. The deal, announced on Wednesday, November 18, brings in KKR as a new investor in the music rights company. Carlyle Global Credit, which founded Litmus in 2022 alongside music industry executives Hank Forsyth and Dan McCarroll, will keep its majority stake in the company after the deal. Litmus says it now has approximately $1.4 billion in assets under management, with a portfolio of more than 100,000 copyrights and recordings featuring music from Katy Perry, benny blanco, Randy Newman and Keith Urban. The commitments will give Litmus 'additional financial flexibility to pursue acquisitions of music catalogs and related rights over the coming years', the company said. KKR is investing primarily through its Asset-Based Finance Partners II fund, and Carlyle's capital comes from its Credit Opportunities strategy, which has deployed more than $6.1 billion across sports, music, television, film and related services since 2017. The deal is the latest sign of how much institutional money is flowing into music rights as an asset class.

articles.title: CMA Awards 2026: the complete winners list
articles.description: The 2026 CMA Awards took place on Wednesday night, and Rolling Stone has the complete winners list. Ella Langley's 'Dandelion' took Album of the Year, Taylor Swift honoured Brooks & Dunn, and the night featured performances from Lainey Wilson, Stephen Wilson Jr. with Chris Stapleton, and a ferocious Brooks & Dunn tribute.
articles.body: The 2026 CMA Awards took place on Wednesday night, and Rolling Stone has the complete winners list. Ella Langley's 'Dandelion' was named Album of the Year, capping a year in which Langley also set the all-time Hot 100 record with 28 weeks at No. 1. Taylor Swift honoured Brooks & Dunn, calling them 'eternal bangers', and threw it back with a performance of her early hit 'Our Song'. Miranda Lambert and Ella Langley gave the live debut of 'Snakeskin Boots', Lainey Wilson debuted a new song with an all-female band, and Stephen Wilson Jr. performed 'I'm a Song' with Chris Stapleton. The night's biggest set piece was the tribute to Brooks & Dunn, with Halestorm, Brothers Osborne, Hardy, Marcus King and Luke Bryan leading the homage to the country duo. The full winners list covers every category from the night.

articles.title: Al Jardine writes open letter to fellow Beach Boy Mike Love: 'Praying for your recovery'
articles.description: Beach Boys co-founder Al Jardine has written an open letter to his bandmate Mike Love, saying he is 'praying for your recovery'. The letter is a rare public message between the two men, whose relationship has been strained for decades.
articles.body: Beach Boys co-founder Al Jardine has written an open letter to his fellow Beach Boy Mike Love, saying he is 'praying for your recovery'. The letter is a rare public message between the two men, whose relationship has been strained for decades — most famously over the band's name, touring rights and creative direction. Jardine's note is warm and direct, and it comes as Love deals with a health issue that has not been detailed publicly. For fans of the band, the letter is a reminder of how long and how complicated the Beach Boys' story is: two men who have been making music together, on and off, for more than sixty years, and who still have things to say to each other in public.

articles.title: John Mayer transports Michael J. Fox Back to the Future with Chuck Berry performance
articles.description: John Mayer gave Michael J. Fox a Back to the Future moment, performing Chuck Berry for the actor whose character made 'Johnny B. Goode' famous in the film. The performance is a sweet collision of two eras of pop culture.
articles.body: John Mayer transported Michael J. Fox Back to the Future with a performance of Chuck Berry, Rolling Stone reports. The moment is a deliberate callback to the 1985 film, in which Fox's Marty McFly plays 'Johnny B. Goode' at the Enchantment Under the Sea dance — a scene that made the Chuck Berry song a shorthand for time travel itself. Mayer's performance, with Fox in the audience, turns the reference into a live event: the guitarist playing the song for the actor who made it iconic on screen. It is a small, sweet collision of two eras of pop culture, and a reminder of how durable the film's musical moment has become forty years on.

articles.title: Harry Styles, Billie Eilish, Cher to headline Glastonbury 2027
articles.description: Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Cher are set to headline Glastonbury 2027, Rolling Stone reports. The lineup pairs two of the biggest pop stars of the moment with a legend — Cher, who would be one of the oldest headliners in the festival's history.
articles.body: Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Cher are set to headline Glastonbury 2027, Rolling Stone reports. The lineup pairs two of the biggest pop stars of the moment with a genuine legend: Cher, who would be one of the oldest headliners in the festival's history, and whose appearance would be a major event in itself. Styles and Eilish are both returning headliners-in-waiting — Styles, who was notably blanked in the 2027 Grammy nominations, and Eilish, who remains one of the defining live acts of her generation. The announcement is the first major festival news of the 2027 season, and it sets the bar for the summer's lineups.

articles.title: Halestorm, Brothers Osborne, Hardy sing for Brooks & Dunn at ferocious CMA tribute
articles.description: Halestorm, Brothers Osborne and Hardy led a ferocious tribute to Brooks & Dunn at the 2026 CMA Awards, backed by Marcus King and Luke Bryan. The hard-rock band also backed the country acts as they paid homage to the duo of Kix Brooks and Ronnie Dunn.
articles.body: Halestorm, Brothers Osborne and Hardy sang for Brooks & Dunn at a ferocious tribute during the 2026 CMA Awards. The hard-rock band also backed Brothers Osborne, Marcus King and Luke Bryan as they paid homage to the country duo of Kix Brooks and Ronnie Dunn. The performance was one of the night's highlights: a loud, guitar-heavy celebration of a duo whose songs have defined country radio for three decades. Taylor Swift also honoured Brooks & Dunn during the ceremony, calling them 'eternal bangers'. The tribute underlined how much of modern country — from hard rock to traditional honky-tonk — runs through the duo's catalogue.

articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters soundtrack sets record with 67 weeks at No. 1
articles.description: The 'KPop Demon Hunters' soundtrack has made Billboard chart history, becoming the soundtrack with the most weeks at No. 1 on the Top Soundtracks chart — 67 weeks, passing the previous record of 62 held by Disney's 'Moana'. Its hit 'Golden' also spent eight nonconsecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Hot 100.
articles.body: The 'KPop Demon Hunters' soundtrack has made Billboard chart history, becoming the soundtrack with the most weeks at No. 1 on the Top Soundtracks chart. According to Billboard's November 3 chart update, the soundtrack from Netflix's animated film has spent 67 weeks in the top position, surpassing the previous record of 62 weeks held by Disney's 'Moana'. Billboard launched the Top Soundtracks chart in June 2001 to track albums connected to movies, television and other screen properties, so the record spans nearly a quarter-century of soundtracks. The soundtrack's success extends beyond the album chart: its hit song 'Golden', performed by the fictional K-pop group HUNTR/X, also reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, spending eight nonconsecutive weeks at the top.

articles.title: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' takes a second Mariah Carey record at 28 weeks
articles.description: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' is No. 1 on the Hot 100 for a 28th week — the longest reign in the chart's history — and this time it took a second Mariah Carey record with it. The song also retook No. 1 on Streaming Songs and is spending a record-extending 21st week atop Digital Song Sales. Her album 'Dandelion' was named CMA Album of the Year.
articles.body: The longest reign in Hot 100 history got longer on Monday, and this time it took a second Mariah Carey record with it. Billboard reported the chart dated November 21: Ella Langley's 'Choosin' Texas' is No. 1 for a 28th week. Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' sits second at 22 weeks, six behind. The week's numbers, from Luminate data for the tracking week of November 6–12: 17.8 million official streams, down 5% on the week; 48.7 million radio airplay audience impressions, down 8%; and 4,000 sold, up 7%. The quieter record fell on the component charts: 'Choosin' Texas' rebounded to No. 1 on Streaming Songs, breaking its tie with 'All I Want for Christmas Is You', and it is spending a record-extending 21st week atop Digital Song Sales. Billboard's updated list of the longest-leading Hot 100 hits now reads: 28 weeks for 'Choosin' Texas'; 22 for 'All I Want for Christmas Is You'; 19 each for Shaboozey's 'A Bar Song (Tipsy)' and Lil Nas X's 'Old Town Road'. The album underneath it, 'Dandelion', was named CMA Album of the Year on Wednesday night. The next Hot 100, dated November 28, either prints 29 or closes the longest reign the chart has recorded.

articles.title: Korn's 'Reward the Scars' climbs to No. 2, blocked from No. 1 by MGK and Fred Durst
articles.description: Korn nearly earns its second No. 1 on Billboard's Hard Rock Digital Song Sales chart as 'Reward the Scars' — its collaboration with the Diablo IV game — jumps to No. 2, blocked by MGK and Fred Durst's 'Fix Ur Face'. The track also debuts at No. 3 on Hot Hard Rock Songs.
articles.body: Korn nearly earns its second No. 1 on Billboard's Hard Rock Digital Song Sales chart as 'Reward the Scars' jumps to No. 2. The song is a collaboration with the Diablo video game series: it accompanies Diablo IV: Lord of Hatred, and it debuted at No. 9 on the chart last week before climbing to second. Only one single keeps Korn from a new chart-topper: MGK — formerly Machine Gun Kelly — recruited Limp Bizkit frontman Fred Durst for 'Fix Ur Face', which leads the sales ranking for a second week. Korn has racked up 13 top 10 hits on the Hard Rock Digital Song Sales chart but only one No. 1 so far — 'Narcissistic Cannibal' — and 'Reward the Scars' is now the fifth single by the band to miss the top by one place. The track also launches at No. 3 on the Hot Hard Rock Songs chart and opens at No. 10 on Alternative Digital Song Sales, Korn's third top 10 there.

articles.title: John Legend's 'Muse' — all 16 songs produced by Pharrell — lands Top 3 on Billboard charts
articles.description: John Legend is back: his new album 'Muse' has landed in the Top 3 on multiple Billboard charts — No. 2 on Top Current Album Sales, No. 2 on Vinyl Albums and No. 3 on Top Album Sales. Every one of the 16 songs was produced by Pharrell Williams, recorded in Paris after more than 20 years of friendship. Fifteen thousand units in week one is his biggest first-week sales in a decade.
articles.body: John Legend is back. His new album 'Muse' has landed in the Top 3 on multiple Billboard charts — No. 2 on Top Current Album Sales, No. 2 on Vinyl Albums and No. 3 on Top Album Sales. Every one of the 16 songs was produced by Pharrell Williams, recorded in Paris after more than 20 years of friendship between the two artists. Fifteen thousand units in the first week is Legend's biggest first-week sales total in a decade. The album is a deliberate throwback to the classic soul record: a tight 16-track set, produced by a single collaborator, with no featured-artist sprawl. For Legend, whose commercial peak was a decade ago, it is a genuine comeback — and a reminder that the album chart still has room for a well-made, old-fashioned record.

articles.title: Olivia Rodrigo's first holiday song debuts at No. 32 as Christmas floods the Hot 100
articles.description: Olivia Rodrigo has debuted her first holiday song, 'Take Me Home (4 Christmas)', at No. 32 on the Hot 100. Eight holiday songs are already in the top 50, led by Wham!'s 'Last Christmas' at No. 14 and Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' at No. 18.
articles.body: Christmas has arrived early on the charts. Eight holiday songs already hold spots in the Billboard Hot 100's top 50, and the newest arrival is Olivia Rodrigo's first-ever holiday song, 'Take Me Home (4 Christmas)', which debuts at No. 32. Wham!'s 'Last Christmas' leads the seasonal pack, jumping from No. 37 to No. 14, while Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' climbs from No. 39 to No. 18 — Wham! pulling a little farther ahead of Carey this week. Bobby Helms' 'Jingle Bell Rock' re-enters at No. 28, reaching its 69th total week on the chart nearly 70 years after its release, and Brenda Lee's 'Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree' follows at No. 30. The Hot 100 carries a November 21 date and tracks listening and sales from November 6 to 12, so this is an early snapshot of the season, not a verdict — but the holiday takeover is already under way.

articles.title: CL signs with Teddy's THEBLACKLABEL, first release due this month
articles.description: Singer CL has signed with THEBLACKLABEL, the label founded by producer Teddy in 2015, Billboard reported on November 13. Her first release under the deal arrives this month. Financial terms have not been made public.
articles.body: Singer CL has signed with THEBLACKLABEL, the label founded by producer Teddy in 2015, Billboard reported on November 13. Her first release under the deal arrives this month, though the report did not give its title, format or release day. Financial terms have not been made public. The move puts the former 2NE1 leader with one of K-pop's most influential producers: Teddy built his reputation crafting hits for BLACKPINK, BIGBANG and 2NE1 itself, and THEBLACKLABEL has become a home for artists looking for a more producer-led setup. For CL, whose solo career has moved between labels and independent releases, the signing is a fresh start with a heavyweight behind her.

articles.title: "AI DJs Completely Kill My Groove"
articles.author: Lauren Goode
articles.description: A first-person field test of the AI DJ features Spotify and YouTube Music are pushing into everyone's playlists — directly relevant to how music fans actually experience streaming now, and a cautionary tale about AI features that interrupt rather than enhance listening.
articles.body:
WIRED software reporter Lauren Goode, a self-described beta-feature enthusiast who uses YouTube Music as her main streaming service, tried living with the synthetic DJ hosts both YouTube Music and Spotify now build into their apps — and ended up turning both of them off. YouTube's version, called "Beyond the Beat" and available through YouTube Labs, randomly interrupts a queue for about 30 seconds between songs to explain the track, set up a vibe shift, and offer context. Spotify introduced its own AI DJ back in 2023 and expanded it in November 2026 with more host personalities and extra controls over the commentary.

The breaking point came during a pop-divas workout playlist. After a Slayyyter track, YouTube's AI DJ launched into a long, platitude-filled monologue about the next Charli XCX song — mispronouncing the artist's name as "Charli XXC" and offering generic commentary with no real substance. Goode's verdict is that the effect is closer to interruption than curation: stilted banter, confidently wrong song trivia, and filler words like "um" and "like" meant to sound human, all breaking the flow of the music the features are supposed to celebrate. Spotify's version fared no better in her testing, despite its head start and its November expansion to eight English-language voices.

The piece's larger point is about where generative AI is being bolted on. Both features remain optional betas that listeners can disable, and Goode argues that is exactly what most listeners will do: the synthetic hosts strip away the human nuance, serendipity, and cultural context that made radio DJs and human curators valuable in the first place, reducing songs to data points wrapped in awkward small talk. For anyone building or marketing music, it is a useful reality check on the gap between the demo promise of "AI curation" and what listeners actually tolerate.

articles.title: "They left the Kennedy Center to survive. It was an artistic rebirth."
articles.author: Philip Kennicott
articles.description: A vivid account of how the Washington National Opera rebuilt itself from zero after walking away from the Kennedy Center — and why the enforced exile produced better, bolder art. A strong arts-institution story with direct lessons for any independent arts organisation.
articles.body:
President Donald Trump's takeover of the Kennedy Center nearly destroyed the Washington National Opera. After Trump stacked the centre's board with loyalists, had himself appointed chairman in 2025, and then put his own name on the venue — a living memorial to John F. Kennedy — ticket sales fell, and the opera's board concluded there was no viable way to continue an association dating back to the centre's opening in 1971.
